note: Substrate-agnostic class; the original occurred on a non-EVM VM. EVM.md is deliberate: unlike SOLANA.md (which carries an explicit aliasing/require_keys_neq section), EVM.md contains nothing about distinctness, so this case tests whether CORE's own method carries the move rather than the module handing it over. Swap the module to port the case.
blinded_brief: An AMM whose pool contracts are directly callable, deployed in an ecosystem alongside an unrelated lending protocol. Fork/replay at the pinned point. Find how an unprivileged caller takes value, or establish there is no such live path.
class: identity/distinctness (Lens E mirror): an operation takes two references of the same kind and the accounting assumes they differ; nothing enforces it. Q2 unbacked-credit at the exit.
must_reach: Enumerates the exits and records the value-moving operation's PARAMETER LIST, not just its name — i.e. notices it takes two or more references of the same kind (two assets/pools/positions, or a source and a destination).
Asks what happens when the caller supplies the SAME reference for both — treats the pair as something to test rather than assuming the general case, before any economics.

Establishes that no on-chain line enforces the two references differ: searches the pool/vault contract itself for the check and records its ABSENCE, and does not accept a router, frontend, or convention as the guard on a directly-callable contract.

Traces the accounting under the aliased call and shows value is credited that was never deposited — one leg is read while the other is written, or one leg's debit is returned by the other's credit, so reserves/shares desync from real holdings (conservation broken).
Proves on the fork: calls the operation with the same reference on both sides, asserts the conservation/reserve invariant is violated, and nets the attacker positive after all real costs.
must_not: Names the specific protocol/incident before making any on-chain/code observation.
Clears the operation because both references are legitimate, registered, non-counterfeit assets — i.e. asks only the forgery half of the identity question and never the distinctness half.
Requires the external funding protocol to be flawed for the path to count; the flash-loan source is correct code and is not the finding.
Accepts an off-chain router or UI that never submits an aliased call as evidence the on-chain path is closed.
Reports the pool as clean because the constant-product / share-price check is present and correct as written — it is, for every input where the two references differ.
answer_for_grader_only: CometDEX 'Comet' AMM on Stellar/Soroban (~$717k, 2025). A swap routed with tokenIn == tokenOut: the pool's accounting was written assuming the two sides are different assets, so the same-asset route credited value never added; attacker flash-funded from Blend, an unrelated lending protocol whose contracts were entirely correct. Found by an attacker in ~36 iterations of poking the live system. Generalizes: any operation over two same-kind references (send/receive account, source/destination, two pools, two positions, members of an aggregate) where distinctness is assumed and unenforced. Note the FP trap: Blend was clean, and the AMM's constant-product check is correct for every non-aliased input.
